thesis: Annie Duke argues that decision-making in poker is fundamentally similar to how children learn language because both involve extracting signal from noise when feedback is delayed or misleading. She explains that outcomes like winning or losing a hand do not always reflect skill, creating a noisy environment where one must distinguish between luck and ability to improve as a decision maker.
